title: Olten ERP - Complete Customer User Guide
subtitle: From first-time setup to delivery, accounting, service and payroll
overview: Follow this handbook in order when setting up a new organization. Once setup is complete, use the workflow maps and chapter headings to find a daily task. Screenshots show synthetic training records, not a customer's live information. Buttons are shown only when the signed-in account has the required access. Save each record and check the success message before proceeding to the next module. New accounting screens require the matching app release; contact your administrator if a screen described here is missing.

chapters.title: 1. Sign in and choose the organization
chapters.purpose: Start in the correct company before creating any customer, stock or accounting record.
before: Obtain your own username and password from the administrator.
Confirm which company workspace you should use.
steps: Open the app address supplied by your administrator. Enter Username and Password, then select Access Systems.
On Select Organization, select your assigned company card. The training screenshots use Demo Medical Trading.
Confirm the organization name in the workspace heading before opening a module.
Use Switch Org to return to company selection when changing organizations. Use Logout or Secure Logout when finished.
chapters.result: The company workspace displays the modules available to your account.
notes: No workspaces assigned means your administrator must grant company access. A missing module can also mean the account lacks its permission.
If the session expires, sign in again. For a connection warning, restore the connection and use Retry connection before repeating a save.

connections.Comes from: Administrator-created account
connections.Next module: User access setup, then Books initialization

screenshots.caption: Enter your own credentials and select Access Systems.
Select the organization that owns the records you will enter.

chapters.title: 2. Add and govern a company workspace
chapters.purpose: Separate each organization's operational and financial records before staff begin using the app.
before: Agree the official workspace name and who should have access.
steps: From Select Organization, select Add Company.
In Register Workspace, enter Organization Name and select Save Org. Wait for the saved company to appear.
Open Manage Users and assign this company under Allowed Companies & Workspaces for each authorized user.
For financial staff, configure the required ERP roles, module clearances and per-company Approval limits (PHP).
Select the company and initialize its standard chart of accounts before its first financial posting. Create the company's master records rather than assuming another company's records are shared.

Use Switch Org and verify the company heading whenever moving between organizations. Limit workspace deletion to an explicitly approved cleanup and read the confirmation and any history-protection rejection.
chapters.result: The organization has a separate workspace, assigned staff and its own operational/accounting setup.
notes: Workspace deletion also concerns its associated document storage folder. It is not a routine way to close an accounting period.
Financial/service history protects the company identity from deletion. Do not remove a live organization to resolve an ordinary data-entry mistake.

connections.Comes from: New organization decision
connections.Next module: User access, Books initialization and master records

screenshots.caption: Create the company, then grant access before staff enter records.
Each company's Finance approval authority must be configured explicitly.

chapters.title: 3. Create staff accounts and assign access
chapters.purpose: Give each staff member the companies, modules and responsibilities needed for their work.
before: Prepare the staff username, account role, company memberships and approved responsibilities.
steps: From Select Organization, select Manage Users. Select + Register New Account, or edit an existing account.
Enter Username and Password. Choose Account Role and Account Status. When editing, leave Password blank to retain it.
Under Module Access Clearances, enable only the required modules. Finance responsibilities need the relevant Finance or Books module as well as an ERP role.
Select the applicable ERP roles: Management, Purchasing, Importation, Warehouse, QC/Regulatory, Sales, Delivery, Finance, Auditor or AI.
Under Allowed Companies & Workspaces, select each permitted company. For Finance, enter a positive Approval limit per company (PHP). Save the account.
Have the staff member sign in and confirm the expected workspace cards appear.
chapters.result: The staff member can use the permitted modules in the assigned companies.
notes: An Admin account alone does not grant the new financial privileges. Auditor is read-only, even when another ERP role is also selected.
Finance requires a configured positive company limit for approvals. A blank Management limit permits its authorized approvals without an amount cap; set a limit when company policy requires one.

connections.Comes from: Company and staff responsibility decisions
connections.Next module: Books setup and operational master records

screenshots.caption: Access & Governance lists registered accounts.
Assign module access and company permissions.
Choose ERP responsibilities and company approval limits.

chapters.title: 4. Initialize the chart of accounts first
chapters.roles: Authorized Finance or Management user with Books access; Super Admin
chapters.purpose: Prepare the standard ledger accounts before posting bills, invoices or payments.
before: Complete company access and financial role setup.
Agree how opening balances and historical invoices will be handled before starting live accounting.
steps: Open Books & Reconciliation from the company workspace. Stay on Accounts & journals.
In Chart of accounts, select Initialize standard accounts. Wait for Default accounting accounts are ready.

Review the standard accounts. They cover Bank, Inventory, Receivables, Input VAT, Payables, Output VAT, accrued landed costs, Equity, Revenue, import expenses, cost of goods sold and service expenses.
To add a company-specific account, expand Add ledger account. Enter a unique Account code, Account name and Account type: ASSET, LIABILITY, EQUITY, REVENUE or EXPENSE.

Save, then confirm the new account appears in the chart. Use it in an approved manual journal or choose it as a compatible POSTING_ROLE target under Account mappings when the company's accounting setup requires it.

Review Account mappings before the first automatic posting. Leave the standard defaults when no remapping is needed. In Cash flow classification, review which asset accounts are designated as cash/bank before relying on cash reports.
chapters.result: The company has its standard accounts and any required custom accounts.
notes: Books is internal accounting; it does not connect to an external QuickBooks subscription.
Only the global Super Admin can delete or restore ledger accounts. A deleted unused standard account can be recreated when an automatic posting needs it.
Opening manual journals affect Books balances. They do not create customer invoices, supplier bills or invoice aging. Arrange a reviewed historical balance migration separately.

connections.Comes from: Role and company setup
connections.Next module: Customers, suppliers, product catalog and warehouse setup

screenshots.caption: Initialize and review the standard chart of accounts.
Add a custom account with the correct account type.

chapters.title: 5. Delete, archive or restore an account
chapters.purpose: Remove an unused account or archive a used account while preserving its accounting history.
before: Sign in as the global Super Admin and select the correct company.
Confirm the account is no longer needed. Review its journals, posting roles, reference mappings, cash/bank designations and bank reconciliations before proceeding.
steps: Open Books & Reconciliation, then Accounts & journals.
Locate the account in Chart of accounts. Check its code and name carefully; Delete is available for standard and custom accounts to the global Super Admin.

Select Delete, read the confirmation and confirm only when it is the intended account. An unused account is permanently removed; an account referenced by journals, mappings or reconciliations is archived instead.
Wait for the success message, then verify the account is absent from the active chart. Existing journals, balances, reports and reconciliation history remain available for archived accounts.
To bring back an archived account, enable Show archived accounts, locate its row and select Restore. Verify that it returns to the active chart before using it for new transactions.
chapters.result: The unused account is removed, or the used account is archived with its history intact. Delete and Restore actions remain in the audit log.
notes: Archived accounts cannot receive new postings or appear as new bank-match candidates. Existing reconciliation matches and historical reports are retained.

Unused accounts can be deleted regardless of code, including the twelve standard accounts. Automatic posting can recreate a missing standard account when needed; restore an archived standard account before using it again.
Deleting an account is not a way to reverse a posted journal. Use an authorized correcting journal for an accounting correction.

Review active posting-role targets and cash/bank designations before archiving. A mapping to an archived account blocks new postings until Finance restores the account or selects a valid replacement. Existing source journals and their verified clearing accounts remain part of history.

connections.Comes from: Account setup or review of an existing ledger account
connections.Next module: Continue master-record setup or review journals

screenshots.caption: Show archived accounts to review retained accounts; only the global Super Admin can select Restore.

chapters.title: 6. Understand the connected workspace
chapters.purpose: Understand where records start and where the next person continues the work.
before: Initialize accounts and grant each team member the appropriate access.
steps: Use the collapsible side navigation and module search to find a workspace. Check the company context and page heading before entering records; expand the mobile menu when the side navigation is hidden.
Use Customer Directory, Supplier Directory and Master Inventory to prepare reusable master records before entering transactions.
For a customer request, start with Create Order Slip. The resulting order feeds P.O. > Fulfillment and Delivery & Proof of Delivery.
If stock must be purchased, use P.O. for supplier procurement, and Importation & Receiving for shipment, customs and inspected receipt.
Use Warehouse & Cycle Counts to locate goods, place accepted receipts, maintain conditions and count stock.
After dispatch and signed POD, create and post the customer invoice in Landed Cost & Finance. Use Books & Reconciliation to inspect the resulting accounting.

Use Books & Reconciliation for Account mappings, Financial statements, Cash flow classification, Inventory reconciliation and Bank reconciliation. Inventory reconciliation requires both Books and Finance read access.
Use Medical Device Service for delivered serials; Executive Dashboard for reports; AI Docs Engine for documents; Payroll Engine for the separate staff-pay workflow.
chapters.result: Each team knows which saved record the next module needs.
notes: The running training example uses Northstar Demo Hospital, Global Demo Medical Supplies and Patient Monitor Demo Model.
Customer fulfillment starts from an Order Slip. Supplier procurement and customer fulfillment share one P.O. workspace but remain different transaction types.

connections.Comes from: Configured company workspace
connections.Next module: Master records, then the connected worked example

screenshots.caption: Use the company workspace, side navigation and search to reach each connected module.

chapters.title: 7. Register the customer and pricing category
chapters.roles: User with Sales access; category management where authorized
chapters.purpose: Create the hospital/customer identity that will be reused by orders, invoices, payments and service records.
before: Prepare the customer's official name, address, contact details, tax identifier and agreed credit limit.
steps: Open Customer Directory. Search Name, Code, Phone first to avoid creating a duplicate.
Select the register action (+ Register on a narrow screen). Enter the customer's name and required contact details.
Enter the address, TIN and optional phone, email and website. Choose the agreed category and credit limit, then save.
If authorized, open Category & Pricing to create a customer category and maintain category prices. Review any percentage change before saving.
Find Northstar Demo Hospital in the directory and open its profile. Confirm the details before selecting its order-slip action.
When Finance access is available, review the profile's new finance balance panel separately from any legacy balance field.
chapters.result: The customer can be selected in Create Order Slip and remains linked through fulfillment and billing.
notes: A customer category can determine the product selling price used when preparing an order. Review the displayed unit price before issuing a document.
Existing legacy balances are not automatically imported into the new invoice aging totals.

connections.Comes from: Customer onboarding details
connections.Next module: Create Order Slip; later invoice, receipt and service

screenshots.caption: Search the directory before registering a new customer.
Complete the customer identity and category fields.

chapters.title: 8. Register products and review prices
chapters.roles: User with Master Inventory access; restricted actions require administrator authority
chapters.purpose: Create the product identity used by purchasing, receiving, reservation, dispatch and costing.
before: Agree a unique SKU, product description, category, manual cost and selling prices.
Create customer categories before setting category-specific overrides.
steps: Open Master Inventory and Product Catalog. Search SKU or Name to avoid duplicating a product.
Select + Register Item. Enter SKU, product name and the required specifications. Set the product category and CMDN where applicable.
Enter the manual Cost Price and selling price. Set Customer Category Pricing Overrides only when an agreed tier price is needed.
Review any Initial Master / Office Audit quantity before saving. For incoming purchases, receive through the proper receiving workflow instead of adding the same goods as initial stock.
Use product-category, customer-tier and hub filters to inspect the catalog. Use Prev / Next for the paginated list.
When Finance access is available, review approved landed-cost reference and cost history without replacing the manual cost or selling-price decision.
chapters.result: Patient Monitor Demo Model has one reusable catalog record and appears in searchable product selectors.
notes: Available stock for an order depends on reservation and lot condition, not just a catalog total.
Set batch/expiry and serial tracking controls in Warehouse & Cycle Counts before handling controlled goods.

connections.Comes from: Approved product specifications and pricing
connections.Next module: Supplier catalog, warehouse controls, QR labels and customer OS

screenshots.caption: Catalog search, category filters, tier prices and stock.
Product identity, manual costs and category-price overrides.

chapters.title: 9. Use catalog Excel import and export safely
chapters.purpose: Load or update multiple catalog rows using the app's existing spreadsheet format.
before: Prepare a reviewed spreadsheet and export the current catalog before a bulk update.
Confirm that each SKU points to the intended product.
steps: Open Product Catalog and select Export Excel to keep a current reference copy.
Select Get Template. Keep the template headings: SKU, Product Name, Master Stock and Cost Price (₱). Replace the example row with your reviewed data.
Use one row per intended SKU and confirm stock quantities and costs before uploading. Save the file as Excel or CSV.
Select Import Excel, choose the file and read the confirmation explaining how existing SKUs will be updated.
Confirm only after review. Wait for the Import complete message and check the Success and Errors counts.
Search a sample of imported SKUs and inspect names, costs and quantities. Correct reported error rows before importing them again.
chapters.result: New SKUs are created and matching existing SKUs receive the imported updates.
notes: This import can update existing product names, manual costs and stock. It is not an append-only operation.
Do not import receipt quantities that have already been received through GRN, warehouse placement or another stock movement.

connections.Comes from: Reviewed catalog spreadsheet
connections.Next module: Catalog verification, warehouse records and operational orders

screenshots.caption: Get Template, Import Excel and Export Excel are on the catalog toolbar.

chapters.title: 10. Register the supplier and assigned products
chapters.purpose: Prepare the vendor identity and supplier-specific cost list for purchase orders and bills.
before: Collect legal name, TIN, complete address, payment terms and contact details.
steps: Open Supplier Directory and check Approved Vendors for an existing record.
Select + Register Supplier. Enter Legal Name, Brand / Trade Name where applicable, TIN / Tax ID and Complete Address.
Add contact person, phone, email and payment terms, then save the profile.
After products exist in Master Inventory, select the supplier's Products button to open Supplier Catalog Link.
Search the master catalog by Name or SKU. Tick products supplied by this vendor and enter the agreed Custom Cost.
Select Save & Sync Catalog. Return to the directory and confirm the assigned-item count.
chapters.result: Global Demo Medical Supplies can be selected for procurement and supplier billing.
notes: Supplier-specific cost is a purchasing reference; it is separate from the customer's selling price.
The directory's legacy A/P Balance is separate from balances calculated from posted bills in the new Finance module.

connections.Comes from: Vendor onboarding and product catalog
connections.Next module: Supplier PO, quotation comparison and supplier bill

screenshots.caption: Supplier directory, terms and assigned products.
Register the vendor's legal and contact details.

chapters.title: 11. Create facilities, bins and tracking controls
chapters.module: Master Inventory and Warehouse & Cycle Counts
chapters.roles: Warehouse user; administrator or warehouse approver for product controls
chapters.purpose: Give stock a physical home before receiving and allocating controlled items.
before: Agree facility names and a consistent building-to-bin naming scheme.
Create the product catalog records.
steps: Open Master Inventory, select its Warehouses view and register each facility with Facility Name and Physical Address.
Return to the workspace and open Warehouse & Cycle Counts. Expand Create a six-level bin.
Choose Facility and enter Building, Floor, Zone, Rack, Shelf and Bin. Select Create bin.
Use a consistent example such as WH1 / F2 / ZA / R03 / S02 / B04. Confirm the resulting code in Warehouse bin hierarchy.
Expand Product tracking controls. Select the product and configure expiry-controlled and serial-controlled handling as applicable; save with an authorized approver.
For existing stock already recorded in the system, use Register existing stock in a bin / batch to locate it. Imported receipts instead use Place QC-accepted goods in a bin after inspection.
chapters.result: Facilities and six-level bin locations are ready for receipt placement, FEFO picking and physical counts.
notes: Registering existing stock in a bin identifies stock already on hand; it must not duplicate a new receipt.
Serial-controlled placement uses one unit per serial. Record the real batch and expiry for expiry-controlled items.

connections.Comes from: Facility plan and catalog tracking decisions
connections.Next module: QR labels, receiving placement, reservation and picking

screenshots.caption: Maintain warehouse facilities in Master Inventory.
Create a bin using the six physical location levels.

chapters.title: 12. Generate labels and use the scanner
chapters.roles: Authorized QR user; administrator verification for database generation or regeneration
chapters.purpose: Print readable product labels and use the same product identity in stock counts, transfers and picking.
before: Save the product catalog and connect the intended label printer or barcode scanner.
steps: Open QR Generator. Search SKU or Name and use All Products or Pending QRs to find the product.
Select Generate Missing when labels are missing. Complete Admin Verification when requested. Regenerate (Admin) is for an authorized regeneration.
Confirm a QR appears for the intended SKU and description. Select Print on that product row.
Choose the label printer in the browser print dialog, check paper size and print a test label before a batch.
In a warehouse count, transfer or delivery pick, scan the sticker into the relevant scan field. Check the selected product before confirming the action.
For controlled goods, also inspect the physical batch, serial and bin. Enter those values where requested.
chapters.result: A product label can identify the catalog product during warehouse work.
notes: A product QR identifies the SKU. It does not by itself prove a particular serial, batch, expiry or bin.
Scanning identifies or fills a product; the workflow's Confirm action is still required to save the business transaction.

connections.Comes from: Saved product catalog
connections.Next module: Stock placement, transfer, cycle count and FEFO pick verification

screenshots.caption: Search products, generate missing QR records and print the required label.

chapters.title: 13. Start the customer request with an Order Slip
chapters.purpose: Capture the customer's demand once, before procurement or delivery work begins.
before: Create Northstar Demo Hospital and the requested products.
Check whether usable stock already exists. If it does, follow the in-stock shortcut after saving the OS.
steps: Open Create Order Slip. Search customer and select Northstar Demo Hospital.
Check the proposed OS number. Search to add the first product and select Patient Monitor Demo Model.
Enter the requested quantity. The main fulfilled example uses one Patient Monitor Demo Model. Review unit prices from the selected customer's category and add any other requested items.
Apply 12% VAT only when appropriate for the document. Review subtotal, VAT and total before generating the Order Slip.

Save/generate the OS and record the actual saved number shown in the success view. Numbers shown before saving are suggestions; if another user saves that number first, the app advances to an available number. A saved document keeps its number. The main fulfilled example is OS-1001. Use Print Order Slip when a copy is required.

If sufficient eligible stock is already available, proceed to Approve & reserve. If stock is missing, retain the OS as the source demand and continue to supplier procurement; reserve after accepted stock is available.
chapters.result: One saved OS records the customer, items, quantities, prices and tax choice.
notes: Generating a document does not issue physical stock. Approval reserves eligible stock; dispatch later issues it.
Do not create another standalone customer PO for the same request. The fulfillment record is derived from this OS.

connections.Comes from: Customer and catalog records
connections.Next module: Supplier procurement when short of stock; otherwise approval/reservation and FO/PL

screenshots.caption: Separate entry example: ten Sterile Syringe 5 mL units. The main fulfillment example uses one monitor on OS-1001.
Separate generated example OS-1002 for ten syringes (PHP 257.60). The same approval and document controls apply to the main OS-1001 example.

chapters.title: 14. Create the supplier PO from the OS demand
chapters.purpose: Order the goods that are missing for an existing customer request, using the shared P.O. workspace.
before: Save the source OS and prepare the selected supplier's catalog and costs.
Decide whether this purchase will use ordinary local delivery verification or the importation/GRN route.
steps: Open P.O. and select Generate P.O. Choose Global Demo Medical Supplies under Select Supplier.
Enter the saved Source O.S., for example OS-1001. Confirm it belongs to this company and represents the customer's demand.

Review the proposed P.O. Number. It continues from the last saved numeric seed; if an authorized user enters another starting number, check it carefully. If the suggestion is already taken when saved, the app advances to an available number. Record the actual number shown in P.O. Ledger.
Review automatically assigned supplier items. Enter the required quantities and vendor unit costs; use + Add Ad-hoc Row only when a needed item is absent.
Set Apply 12% VAT when appropriate, review the totals, then select Issue Purchase Order.
Open P.O. Ledger and View the saved PO. For ordinary purchases use Verify Delivery when the goods arrive. If marked Receive in Importation / GRN & QC, continue through that controlled import route.
chapters.result: The supplier PO records what the business is buying and retains its source OS reference.
notes: Generate P.O. and P.O. Ledger concern purchases from suppliers. Fulfillment concerns the customer order generated from the OS. They share a workspace, not the same stock movement.
Do not receive imported goods once here and again through GRN.

connections.Comes from: Saved customer OS and supplier catalog
connections.Next module: Shipment planning / GRN for imports, or local Verify Delivery and placement

screenshots.caption: Select the supplier and source OS, then review the incrementing PO number.
The ledger identifies which receiving route applies.

chapters.title: 15. Use requisitions and compare supplier quotations
chapters.roles: Importation or Purchasing staff with module access; authorized requisition approver
chapters.purpose: Record a purchase request and compare supplier offers before committing to an import purchase.
before: Alternative procurement route: skip this create-PO path if the intended supplier PO was already issued in the previous chapter. Use one procurement route for the same quantities.
Prepare product requirements, quantities, purpose, needed-by date and supplier offers.
Use the existing OS demand as the business reference where the purchase fulfills a customer request.
steps: Open Importation & Receiving, choose Requisitions and expand Create purchase requisition. Enter Purpose and Needed by, select products and quantities, then Save requisition to create the draft.
Select the draft request and expand Add supplier quotation. Choose Supplier, Currency, PHP per 1 currency unit, lead time, payment terms and valid-until date.
Enter each quoted unit cost and minimum order quantity, add notes and select Save quotation. Repeat for the competing offers before submitting.
Once at least one quotation is saved, select Submit for approval. Confirm the request becomes Submitted.
The authorized approver compares PHP-converted cost, lead time, terms and minimum quantities in Supplier quotation comparison.
On the chosen quotation, select Approve & create PO. Alternatively Reject the submitted request with a reason. Confirm the generated PO reference before planning the shipment.
chapters.result: The request, approval and supplier offer comparison remain available as the procurement record.
notes: A requisition and a supplier quotation are procurement planning records, not customer invoices or payment records.
Use a single intended procurement route for a purchase. Do not issue a second PO for quantities already ordered.

connections.Comes from: Demand and supplier offers
connections.Next module: Approved supplier PO, import file and shipment

screenshots.caption: Select requests and compare recorded supplier quotations.
Enter purpose, needed-by date, products and requested quantities.

chapters.title: 16. Create the import file and shipment
chapters.purpose: Track which ordered quantities are actually shipping, including partial and consolidated supplier POs.
before: Save the supplier PO and obtain shipping details from the supplier or forwarder.
steps: Choose Shipments and expand Create import file. Enter Title and Notes, then select Create import file.
Expand Create shipment (partial or consolidated POs). Select the Import file that groups this import work.
Enter the shipment references, shipping mode, route and planned dates shown in the form.
Choose each Purchase order line and enter Shipped quantity. Add lines for the actual shipment; quantities may cover only part of a PO or several eligible POs.
Select Create shipment. Find the new shipment number, such as SHP-2026-000001, in Shipment tracker.
Use the shipment's Edit action as tracking information changes. Update status, dates and references, then select Save tracking.
chapters.result: The shipment connects supplier PO quantities to customs, receipt inspection and shipment costing.
notes: Shipped quantity is not the same as received or available stock. Customs and QC still need to be recorded.
Keep dates current so delayed-shipment alerts and performance reports reflect the latest known position.

connections.Comes from: Supplier PO lines
connections.Next module: Customs clearance, GRN & QC and landed-cost calculation

screenshots.caption: Create import files, plan shipment quantities and maintain tracking.

chapters.title: 17. Record customs clearance and import expenses
chapters.purpose: Record cleared quantities and the actual import charges needed for receiving and cost review.
before: Create the shipment and collect broker/clearance information and charge documents.
steps: Choose Customs and select the intended Shipment.
Complete Broker & clearance details, Clearance date and Clearance status.
For each item, enter Cleared quantity (cumulative). This is the total cleared so far, not another receipt quantity. Select Save clearance.
In Itemized import expenses, choose a category and enter Description, Currency, Amount, Status and Invoice reference.
Enter Paid date only when the payment really occurred, then select Add expense or Save expense when editing.
Review the expense list against supporting documents and pass the charges to Finance for landed-cost allocation and, where payable, a reviewed supplier/import-expense bill.
chapters.result: The shipment has an auditable clearance position and an itemized operational expense list.
notes: Recording an operational import expense is not a substitute for posting a supplier bill in Finance.
Avoid duplicate charges when linking an import expense to a bill. Landed-cost allocation and supplier liability are separate steps.

connections.Comes from: Shipment and broker documents
connections.Next module: GRN & QC, Finance bill and landed cost

screenshots.caption: Save cumulative clearance quantities and itemized import charges.

chapters.title: 18. Receive cleared goods and record QC
chapters.purpose: Separate accepted, rejected and held goods before warehouse placement or sale.
before: Create and clear the shipment. Physically inspect quantities, packaging, batches, expiry and damage.
steps: Choose GRN & QC, select Shipment and expand Record goods receipt & QC inspection.
Enter Received date and receipt notes. For each line, enter the quantity physically received.
Allocate every received unit to Accepted, Rejected or Hold. For example, 10 received must be fully explained by those three quantities.
Enter batch number and expiration date where applicable. Add damage/missing-item notes and inspection photographs when needed.
Select Save goods receipt. Confirm the generated GRN appears in Goods receipts & quarantine ledger.
For held goods, use the line's QC reinspection action. Record the inspected allocation and notes, then select Save QC decision. Only accepted quantities should proceed to placement.
chapters.result: The GRN records what arrived and distinguishes usable goods from quarantine or rejected quantities.
notes: Accepted stock must be placed through the accepted-receipt queue; do not add it again using a generic stock adjustment.
Rejected or held stock does not become available for customer reservation merely because it has arrived.

connections.Comes from: Cleared shipment quantities
connections.Next module: QC-accepted bin placement; hold/rejected goods remain under QC control

screenshots.caption: The receipt ledger separates accepted, rejected and held quantities.
Receive quantities and capture batch, expiry and inspection evidence.

chapters.title: 19. Upload, organize and search company documents
chapters.purpose: Keep company documents organized and searchable for operational review, reminders and invoice OCR.
before: Ask the administrator to complete the document-storage and AI-service configuration.
Prepare readable source files with clear filenames.
steps: Open AI Docs Engine. Check the company name and wait for the directory to load; use Retry connection if configuration or network access is unavailable.
Select Folder to create a named folder, or select an existing folder in the tree. Root Dir returns to the company's top level.
Select Upload and choose the intended files. Wait for upload, processing and the expiry/reminder review to complete before leaving the page.
Use Filter files locally to narrow the directory. Select a document to inspect its preview and recorded information.
Use the document rename or replacement actions when maintaining an existing source. Review any Delete Selected action carefully because it deletes selected documents/folders.

Type a document question in Ask AI to analyze across all folders and submit it. Compare its answer with the original document preview. For invoice line extraction, continue to Executive AI & Invoice OCR.
chapters.result: Uploaded company documents can be previewed, organized, searched and selected for other permitted document workflows.
notes: The training screenshots show an isolated workspace without a connected Drive account; they illustrate the real controls and connection message, not a completed upload.
Document AI and Executive AI serve different contexts: this module analyzes uploaded documents; Executive AI answers from authorized management reports.

connections.Comes from: Company source files and storage configuration
connections.Next module: Expiry reminders, import-document links and invoice OCR

screenshots.caption: The document workspace offers folders, Upload, local filtering and AI document search.

chapters.title: 20. Review expiry reminders and replace renewed documents
chapters.purpose: Check AI-read expiry information against the source and keep renewal follow-up current.
before: Upload a readable document and wait for processing.
Know the source expiry date and the desired reminder lead time.
steps: After upload, review Review Expiry & Reminder. Use View source document to compare the extracted information with the original.
Correct the date/reminder details shown in the review form. Use Re-analyze if the available extraction is incomplete and the action is offered.
Select Save Reminder only when the dates and schedule are correct. Select Close Without Reminder when no reminder should be created for that file.
Open the Expiry Reminders panel from the notification control and inspect due items.
Use View source document before deciding the next action. Select Mark Handled when the follow-up has been completed.

When renewed evidence replaces an existing document, select Replace Document, choose the new source and complete its review. Confirm the new expiry/reminder details rather than assuming the old schedule is still correct.
chapters.result: The recorded reminder reflects verified source information and completed follow-up is marked handled.
notes: AI-read dates require staff review. A reminder is a follow-up record, not proof that a permit or document has been renewed.
If storage or AI is disconnected, resolve configuration with the administrator before relying on automatic processing.

connections.Comes from: Uploaded documents and verified expiry dates
connections.Next module: Renewal follow-up, document replacement and document-related alerts

screenshots.caption: Review the expiry reminder list and source-document actions.

chapters.title: 21. Link regulatory and shipment documents
chapters.roles: User with the necessary importation and document access
chapters.purpose: Keep supporting documents connected to the appropriate import file, shipment or product.
before: Upload the source documents into the company's AI Docs Engine. Have import file, shipment and product references ready.
steps: Choose Documents in Importation & Receiving and wait for Regulatory & import documents to load.
Find the intended document by its name and review its current type and linked records.
Open its link/edit action. Select the relevant Import file, Shipment and Product where applicable.
Set Regulatory status and Document type to reflect the reviewed source document.
Select Save document links. Confirm the displayed links and status belong to the intended company and shipment.
Maintain expiry/reminder information in AI Docs Engine when the document requires renewal or follow-up.
chapters.result: The same company document can be found in the context of the import, shipment or product it supports.
